patient_selection.evidence: Patients who visited the neurology clinic between August 2022 and February were consecutively enrolled.
patient_selection.rationale: Prospective consecutive enrolment from a defined clinic population with explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria and random assignment to the three scanner vendors.

index_test.evidence: randomized datasets were presented for rating, with reconstruction methods and clinical information blinded by removing and anonymizing the DICOM headers.
index_test.rationale: Readers were blinded to the reconstruction method, cases were presented in randomized order, and the Likert scales were pre-specified.

reference_standard.evidence: A typical randomized crossover design with a 4-week washout period was used [15].
reference_standard.rationale: The conventional acquisition served as the standard-of-care reference and was read by the same blinded readers in a randomized crossover with washout, so reference reading was not informed by the index images.

flow_timing.evidence: The patients underwent both conventional and Accel-DL brain MRI protocols, including 2D axial T1WI, T2WI, T2-FLAIR, and 3D T1WI.
flow_timing.rationale: Every participant received both index and reference acquisitions in the same session (zero interval) and all 150 enrolled participants entered the final analysis.

app_patient_selection.evidence: this prospective evaluation did not include patients with large lesions or structural distortions, such as acute hemorrhage, infarction, or tumors, highlighting the need for further research.
app_patient_selection.rationale: By design the cohort excluded acute focal deficits and the space-occupying pathologies most relevant to whether accelerated reconstruction preserves diagnostic content.

app_index_test.evidence: A DICOM-based U-Net architecture was developed in a supervised manner and trained on numerous image pairs to transform low-quality images from undersampled k-space data into high-quality images
app_index_test.rationale: The index test is a commercial deep-learning reconstruction of prospectively undersampled data giving ~39% scan-time reduction, directly matching the review question.

app_reference_standard.evidence: Conventional and Accel-DL MRI images were obtained from each participant and compared using 2D T1- and T2-weighted and 3D gradient-echo sequences.
app_reference_standard.rationale: The reference is the routine clinical (non-accelerated) acquisition read by neuroradiologists, which matches the review's reference-standard definition.

patient_selection.evidence: Participants were consecutively recruited from March to June 2022 and in November 2023.
patient_selection.rationale: Prospective consecutive recruitment of children referred for clinically indicated brain MRI across a broad range of indications, with no case-control structure.

index_test.evidence: Three blinded radiologists with 10 years (rater 1), 6 years (rater 2), and 3 years (rater 3) of experience independently rated both sequences
index_test.rationale: Readers were stated to be blinded, rated independently, and used a pre-defined 5-point Likert scale with category definitions given in Table 2.

reference_standard.evidence: The T2PROPELLER CS sequence was compared to a conventional, CS-accelerated Cartesian turbo-spin-echo T2-weighted sequence (T2Cartesian CS).
reference_standard.rationale: The comparator is the routine clinical T2 sequence, rated by the same blinded independent readers, so reference interpretation was not informed by knowledge of the index result.

flow_timing.evidence: The T2PROPELLER CS sequence was acquired before the T2Cartesian CS sequence for 4 of the anesthetized patients and after for the remaining patients.
flow_timing.rationale: Both sequences were acquired in the same examination in the same orientation for every patient, and all 31 patients were analysed; only acquisition order varied.

app_patient_selection.evidence: Twenty-one of the 31 patients had lesions, including pre- and post-treatment astrocytic tumors such as pilocytic astrocytomas of the cerebellum
app_patient_selection.rationale: A real clinical brain-MRI population with a high prevalence of genuine pathology, appropriate for judging preservation of diagnostic content.

app_index_test.evidence: Enabling faster and motion-robust MRI of the brain in infants and children using a novel, enhanced compressed sensing (CS) algorithm in combination with a turbo-spin-echo T2-weighted sequence utilizing the PROPELLER-technique
app_index_test.rationale: The index test is an accelerated acquisition/reconstruction (31% shorter scan) evaluated in brain MRI, matching the review question.

app_reference_standard.evidence: Clinically, a Cartesian sampling scheme is most commonly employed for its robust data collection, practical implementation
app_reference_standard.rationale: The comparator is the standard-of-care clinical sequence permitted by the review definition, although it is itself CS-accelerated rather than fully sampled.

patient_selection.evidence: The IXI dataset comprises 580 cases of T1-weighted (T1-w) brain MRI images.
patient_selection.rationale: Retrospective convenience use of two public datasets with no stated patient eligibility criteria, sampling frame, or clinical context.

index_test.evidence: To quantitatively assess the performance of the models in removing brain motion ARTs, we reported three metrics: normalized mean squared error (NMSE), structural similarity index measure (SSIM), and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR).
index_test.rationale: Evaluation was entirely by automated similarity metrics with no reader interpretation, so blinding and pre-specified diagnostic thresholds cannot be assessed.

reference_standard.evidence: This dataset includes three types of images: ground truth motion-free images, motion-corrupted images with a low level of distortion (level 1), and motion-corrupted images with a high level of distortion (level 2).
reference_standard.rationale: Matched motion-free acquisitions (in-vivo) and the original uncorrupted images (in-silico) provide an appropriate paired ground truth applied identically to every case.

flow_timing.evidence: Rigid brain image registration was performed using FSL-FLIRT (Jenkinson and Smith 2001, Jenkinson et al 2002) to compensate for misalignment between the motion-free and motion-corrupted images.
flow_timing.rationale: Fully paired design in which every test case has its own reference; the in-silico corruption is applied to the same data so the interval is zero and no cases were dropped.

app_patient_selection.evidence: Additionally, model performance on in-vivo data was evaluated using the MR-ART T1-w brain MRI dataset, which comprises 148 cases (95 females and 53 males).
app_patient_selection.rationale: Only counts and sex are reported; clinical indication, age and presence of pathology are unstated, so match to a clinical brain-MRI population cannot be judged.

app_index_test.evidence: It is important to note that our study was conducted in the image domain, rather than in k-space.
app_index_test.rationale: The index test is retrospective post-processing of reconstructed magnitude images for motion artefact removal, not an accelerated reconstruction from undersampled acquisition.

app_reference_standard.evidence: We adapted the motion simulation technique of Duffy et al (2021) to generate an in-silico dataset with varying levels of motion ARTs including high, moderate, and minor
app_reference_standard.rationale: The reference is the clean/motion-free acquisition, which satisfies the review's reference-standard definition, although no expert reading of the reference was performed.

patient_selection.evidence: Participants were recruited between October and December 2024. Written informed consent was obtained from all patients’ legal guardians prior to participation in the study.
patient_selection.rationale: Prospective single-centre recruitment over a fixed window, but no statement that enrolment was consecutive or random and no eligibility/exclusion rule is given.

index_test.evidence: all images were analyzed by two radiologists with 4 (rater 1) and 9 (rater 2) years of experience, who independently rated T2-SSHconv- and T2-SSHDL-sequences qualitatively on a five-point Likert scale
index_test.rationale: Ratings were independent and the Likert scale pre-defined, but blinding of the readers to the reconstruction type is never reported.

reference_standard.evidence: the two radiologists compared T2-SSHDL-sequences with high-resolution T2-weighted sequences for the categories artifacts and lesion conspicuity, using the aforementioned five-point Likert scale
reference_standard.rationale: The routine high-resolution T2 sequence is a plausible reference, but it was read in direct paired comparison with the index images and blinding is not described; no pathology-level verification was performed.

flow_timing.evidence: The raw data of these sequences were reconstructed using a prototypical DL-based reconstruction framework provided by the vendor that combines and integrates CS with two different CNNs
flow_timing.rationale: Index and conventional images derive from identical raw data (zero interval) and all 62 enrolled patients contributed to the analysis.

app_patient_selection.evidence: 33 of the 62 patients had lesions, including tumors such as gliomas, astrocytomas, craniopharyngiomas or embryonal tumors with multilayered rosettes
app_patient_selection.rationale: Clinically indicated paediatric brain MRI with a wide indication spectrum and genuine pathology in half the cohort, well matched to the review question.

app_index_test.evidence: This study aimed to evaluate a novel DL-based reconstruction framework for T2-weighted single-shot brain MRI in a pediatric cohort that integrates CS acceleration with convolutional neural networks (CNNs)
app_index_test.rationale: A vendor deep-learning reconstruction of compressed-sensing accelerated raw k-space data, exactly the class of index test the review addresses.

app_reference_standard.evidence: In sedated patients, high-resolution T2-weighted sequences achieved superior image quality and lesion conspicuity, as motion was minimized.
app_reference_standard.rationale: Both comparators (conventional CS reconstruction of the same raw data and routine high-resolution T2) are standard-of-care acquisitions read by radiologists.

patient_selection.evidence: After quality control, the dataset comprised 50 matched uLF–HF pairs, 100 HF-only scans, and 130 uLF-only scans.
patient_selection.rationale: Single-centre retrospective convenience sample with no stated eligibility rule and unspecified quality-control exclusions; the number of distinct neonates is never given.

index_test.evidence: Raters were not shown the original scans; therefore, the study is not clinically applicable, and diagnostic decisions were not permitted due to ethical constraints.
index_test.rationale: Raters saw only model outputs with no comparator and no reference images; scoring categories are minimal (bad/acceptable/good) and no pre-specified diagnostic threshold is described.

reference_standard.evidence: HF data were obtained from multiple clinical 3 T scanners with heterogeneous resolutions
reference_standard.rationale: The high-field reference was acquired on multiple scanners with heterogeneous protocols, and the truth source for the reported pathology-detection accuracy is not described.

flow_timing.evidence: Tests were conducted on 46 matched uLF–HF pairs (34 for LF-SynthSR, which requires T2-weighted input).
flow_timing.rationale: Of 50 matched pairs only 46 were tested and the headline table reports 34, comparator methods were evaluated on different subsets, and the uLF-to-HF acquisition interval is never stated.

app_patient_selection.evidence: The cohort included neonates under six months of age with nine different pathologies.
app_patient_selection.rationale: Real clinical neonatal brain MRI including pathological cases, an appropriate population for judging preservation of diagnostic content.

app_index_test.evidence: We propose MRIQT, a 3D conditional diffusion framework for image quality transfer (IQT) from uLF to HF MRI.
app_index_test.rationale: The index test is generative cross-field-strength image synthesis rather than accelerated reconstruction of the subject's own undersampled data, a substantial mismatch with the review question.

app_reference_standard.evidence: High-field magnetic resonance imaging (HF-MRI) remains the gold standard for structural and functional assessment
app_reference_standard.rationale: 3 T high-field MRI is the accepted standard-of-care reference acquisition anticipated by the review's reference-standard definition.

patient_selection.evidence: All experiments are conducted on the multicoil test split provided by the dataset, restricted to T1-weighted volumes.
patient_selection.rationale: Evaluation relies on convenience use of public dataset splits with no patient-level eligibility criteria, recruitment description, or consecutive/random sampling.

index_test.evidence: For severe motion scans we keep N = 200, while for all remaining scans we use N = 100.
index_test.rationale: A key index-test setting (number of reverse diffusion iterations) was chosen per scan using the reference-derived motion-severity label, so the index test was not pre-specified or applied uniformly; no blinded reader interpretation exists.

reference_standard.evidence: we adopt the same motion severity categorization (mild, moderate, and severe) as in Wang et al. [43] and use the ℓ1-regularized reconstruction of the motion-free scan as the reference.
reference_standard.rationale: The subject's own motion-free acquisition serves as reference and was applied identically to the index method and all baselines with uniform registration, masking and normalisation.

flow_timing.evidence: The dataset provides four scans per subject: one motion-free and three motion-corrupted scans.
flow_timing.rationale: Four scans across 8 subjects implies 32 volumes but only 27 are reported and 24 motion-corrupted scans are analysed, and the missing volumes are not accounted for.

app_patient_selection.evidence: We conduct real-motion experiments using the PMoC3D dataset [43], which comprises 27 volumes from 8 healthy subjects.
app_patient_selection.rationale: Real-motion evaluation uses only healthy volunteers (and public research datasets), so preservation of clinically relevant lesions cannot be assessed.

app_index_test.evidence: we propose a unified Bayesian framework for motion-compensated 3D MRI that jointly estimates the anatomical image, rigid-body motion parameters, and coil sensitivity maps directly from motion-corrupted k-space data
app_index_test.rationale: The index test reconstructs directly from accelerated (R = 4-8) undersampled k-space using a learned diffusion prior, matching the review's index-test definition.

app_reference_standard.evidence: We first generate synthetic inter-shot motion trajectories to corrupt k-space data from the fully sampled FastMRI dataset using 52 acquisition shots. Reconstructions are compared against the original motion-free reference volumes.
app_reference_standard.rationale: Fully sampled motion-free volumes serve as the reference, satisfying the review definition, although no expert radiologist reading of the reference was performed.
